PF2e Tavern Games — Rules Reference

This module currently automates five games: Poppy’s Prize, Golem, Bounder, Century, and a drinking contest. The GM controls table setup and may disqualify any actor in every game. Players with Owner permission on their actor use their private panel for legal actions.

Poppy’s Prize

Poppy’s Prize uses a 54-card deck: 52 suited cards and two Pirates. The GM selects two to four participants, an ante, and Poppy. Poppy deals; each player chooses a face-down common card, followed by betting after each common-card reveal. Pirates can Plunder a matching card from another player. At showdown, the best five-card poker hand wins the pot. Participants may carry one card into the next game.

Golem

Golem is a 52-card, three-to-six player poker game. Each participant antes, receives five cards, and bets from the amulet holder. Active players may discard up to two cards and receive replacements; all discards form the face-down golem hand. After final betting, the best player hand must strictly beat the golem hand to win the pot less the house’s 5% share. If it does not, that player adds twice the ante to the pot and the hand continues. The amulet moves counterclockwise when a pot is won.

Bounder

The Shooter stakes an amount and rolls a first d20 for a point. The Shooter may double the stake. Other players may bet on the point, all odd, all even, or three of a kind. The dealer rolls 3d6, then the Shooter rolls a second d20. The point bet wins when the two d20s bracket the dealer total; a natural 1 and 20 pair doubles only the Shooter’s winnings. The next clockwise eligible participant becomes Shooter.

Century

Each player stakes an amount and chooses two through ten distinct numbers from 1 to 100. The Dealer generates twenty distinct results from two d10. Payout is determined by the official Century table from the number selected and numbers matched; the module displays every player’s match count, multiplier, and payout after the draw.

Drinking Contest

For each round, every contestant presses Ready. Once all qualified contestants are ready, the module makes blind-to-GM Performance and Fortitude checks for each contestant. Compare Fortitude with the GM’s DC: critical success reduces the stage by 1, success has no effect, failure increases it by 1, and critical failure by 2. At Stage 6, a contestant is unconscious for eight hours and eliminated.

StageNameEffect
1Liquid Courage+1 item bonus to saving throws against fear for 10 minutes
2TipsyOff-guard and the Stage 1 bonus for 10 minutes
3SloshedClumsy 1, off-guard, stupefied 2 for 10 minutes
4WobblingClumsy 2 and sickened 2 for 10 minutes
5Blackout BoundClumsy 2, sickened 2, stupefied 2 for 10 minutes
6Passed OutUnconscious for 8 hours; eliminated

Cheating

In Poppy’s Prize and Golem, a dealer with marked-playing-cards may use marked cards. In Bounder, the Shooter with games-loaded-dice may choose each d20 result; in Century, the Dealer with that slug may choose the twenty results. A drinking contestant may cheat to automatically succeed their Fortitude save; their blind Performance result is compared separately with each other contestant’s Perception DC. The GM and each observer who detects cheating receive private notices.

Source acknowledgement. Poppy’s Prize originates in Jewel of the Indigo Isles. Golem, Bounder, and Century originate in Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing, p. 76, as presented by Archives of Nethys. The drinking contest is a table rule supplied for this module.
